title: How Democracy Itself Ended Up on the Ballot in Wisconsin

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·朗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其背后文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在我还在夜店里用黑胶唱片打碟的那个年代，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每天晚上都要带着 300 件最珍贵的宝贝去上班，把 DJ 台变成一个充满活力的快闪博物馆，展示着那些精美的、有 50 年历史的艺术品。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼出品的《重构者》吧。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is A Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《今日报道》。

sentences.en: Over the past decade, Wisconsin has become an extreme experiment in single-party rule.
sentences.zh: 在过去十年里，威斯康星州已成为单党统治的一场极端实验。

sentences.en: Despite being an evenly split swing state, Republican officials there have redrawn the state's election districts and rewritten its laws
sentences.zh: 尽管威斯康星州是一个势均力敌的摇摆州，但那里的共和党官员重新划分了选区并重写了选举法，

sentences.en: to ensure that they disproportionately dominate the state's legislature.
sentences.zh: 以确保他们在州议会中占据绝对的压倒性优势。

sentences.en: Now, those same Republicans are asking voters for the final lever of power.
sentences.zh: 现在，这些共和党人正向选民索要最后的一项权力杠杆：

sentences.en: control over the state's entire system of voting.
sentences.zh: 对全州选举制度的控制权。

sentences.en: Today, my colleagues Reid Epstein, Rob Zipko, and Rachel Quester go to Wisconsin to understand how democracy itself ended up on the ballot.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事里德·爱泼斯坦、罗伯·齐普科和瑞秋·奎斯特前往威斯康星州，去了解民主本身是如何被推上选票的。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, November 8th, Election Day.
sentences.zh: 今天是 11 月 8 日，星期二，选举日。

sentences.en: Reid, my sense is that you have basically moved to Wisconsin over the past few weeks.
sentences.zh: 里德，我的感觉是，过去几周你基本上已经搬到威斯康星州去了。

sentences.en: You're almost a resident.
sentences.zh: 你快成那里的居民了。

sentences.en: Yeah, Michael, this is my fourth trip to Wisconsin in the last month.
sentences.zh: 是的，迈克尔，这是我过去一个月里第四次去威斯康星州了。

sentences.en: Well, explain why.
sentences.zh: 嗯，解释一下原因。

sentences.en: Because it seems to me your beat during these midterms has been, for lack of a better phrase, the state of democracy in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 因为在我看来，你在这次中期选举中的报道重点，用一个词来形容，就是美国的民主状况。

sentences.en: How exactly does Wisconsin fit into that question?
sentences.zh: 威斯康星州究竟是如何卷入这个问题的？

sentences.en: It has seemed for a while that democracy is kind of sitting on a nice edge in Wisconsin.
sentences.zh: 一段时间以来，民主在威斯康星州似乎一直处于一种岌岌可危的边缘状态。

sentences.en: It's a 50-50 state in statewide elections.
sentences.zh: 在全州范围的选举中，这是一个五五开的州。

sentences.en: Four of the last six presidential elections have been decided by less than a percentage point.
sentences.zh: 过去六次总统选举中，有四次的胜负差距不到一个百分点。

sentences.en: But Republicans here control the state legislature with such a tight grip that there's almost no hope of Democrats doing much of anything.
sentences.zh: 但这里的共和党人对州议会的控制非常严密，民主党人几乎没有任何作为的希望。

sentences.en: Other than electing a governor who can veto conservative legislation.
sentences.zh: 除了选出一位可以否决保守派立法的州长之外。

sentences.en: And Governor Tony Evers, who won in the blue wave of 2018 by a whopping 1.1%, is up for re-election against a Republican named Tim Michaels,
sentences.zh: 而托尼·埃弗斯州长，他在 2018 年的“蓝色浪潮”中以 1.1% 的微弱优势获胜，这次他将面临共和党人蒂姆·迈克尔斯的挑战，

sentences.en: who has expressed skepticism about the results of the 2020 election.
sentences.zh: 后者曾对 2020 年的选举结果表示怀疑。

sentences.en: He has said if he wins the election, that Republicans will never lose another election in Wisconsin.
sentences.zh: 他说，如果他赢得选举，共和党人将永远不会在威斯康星州输掉任何一场选举。

sentences.en: And what does he mean by that?
sentences.zh: 他这话是什么意思？

sentences.en: Well, it wasn't clear what he meant at the time.
sentences.zh: 嗯，当时还不清楚他具体指什么。

sentences.en: His campaign aides have since said that what he meant was he would implement policies so popular that it would elect Republicans forever.
sentences.zh: 他的竞选助手后来表示，他的意思是将实施非常受欢迎的政策，从而让共和党人永远当选。

sentences.en: But what Democrats heard him say was that he and Republicans in the legislature would rewrite the state's election laws so that Republicans would never lose again.
sentences.zh: 但民主党人听到的是，他和议会中的共和党人将重写该州的选举法，这样共和党人就永远不会再输了。

sentences.en: Meaning, the new governor and this firmly Republican legislature,
sentences.zh: 也就是说，新州长和这个稳固的共和党议会，

sentences.en: they would literally re-engineer how it is that people in Wisconsin vote to perpetuate their own re-election and power.
sentences.zh: 他们将从字面上重新设计威斯康星州的投票方式，以延续他们自己的连任和权力。

sentences.en: If not necessarily re-engineer how they vote, re-engineer who is in control of the voting and the counting.
sentences.zh: 即使不一定是重新设计投票方式，也是在重新设计谁来控制投票和计票过程。

sentences.en: So now it makes sense how the future of democracy fits into Wisconsin.
sentences.zh: 所以现在明白了，民主的未来是如何与威斯康星州联系在一起的。

sentences.en: That's really what's at stake in the election here today.
sentences.zh: 这确实是今天这里选举中面临的赌注。

sentences.en: So how exactly does Wisconsin find itself in this position?
sentences.zh: 那么威斯康星州究竟是如何陷入这种境地的呢？

sentences.en: Well, to really understand that, you have to go back and take a closer look at how the 2020 election played out here in Wisconsin.
sentences.zh: 嗯，要真正理解这一点，你必须回顾并仔细审视 2020 年的选举在威斯康星州是如何进行的。

sentences.en: So for the past few weeks, I, along with Daily Producers Rob Zipko and Rachel Quester, have been doing just that.
sentences.zh: 在过去的几周里，我和《今日报道》的制片人罗伯·齐普科以及瑞秋·奎斯特一直在做这件事。

sentences.zh: 是从寒冷的地方出来吗？

sentences.en: And one person we talked to who really brought this all into focus for us is a woman named Nikki, who lives in Racine County, about a half hour south of Milwaukee.
sentences.zh: 我们采访的一位真正让我们看清这一切的人，是一位名叫尼基的女士，她住在密尔沃基以南约半小时车程的拉辛县。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Shall we start?
sentences.zh: 我们开始吧？

sentences.en: Let's do it.
sentences.zh: 开始吧。

sentences.en: And tell me about Nikki.
sentences.zh: 跟我说说尼基吧。

sentences.en: What do I need to know?
sentences.zh: 我需要知道些什么？

sentences.en: Well, I was born and raised in Racine.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我在拉辛出生长大。

sentences.en: So, yeah, I pretty much only have known Racine as far as where I've lived.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，就我居住的地方而言，我几乎只了解拉辛。

sentences.en: So Nikki's a small business owner with four kids.
sentences.zh: 尼基是一位有四个孩子的个体经营者。

sentences.en: She's lived in Wisconsin her whole life.
sentences.zh: 她一生都住在威斯康星州。

sentences.en: You know, for somebody who's never been here, if you kind of had to take them by the shoulders and be like, this is what Wisconsin is, this is what Wisconsin's about,
sentences.zh: 你知道，对于一个从未到过这里的人，如果你必须抓住他们的肩膀说，这就是威斯康星，这就是威斯康星的意义所在，

sentences.en: what would you say to them?
sentences.zh: 你会对他们说什么？

sentences.en: Beer.
sentences.zh: 啤酒。

sentences.en: Beer.
sentences.zh: 啤酒。

sentences.en: I mean, if I'm being honest, it is about beer and cheese.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果我诚实地说，这里就是关于啤酒和奶酪。

sentences.en: I'm sure everybody's heard that.
sentences.zh: 我相信每个人都听说过。

sentences.en: But she says she didn't grow up in a particularly political household, but by the time she started her own family.
sentences.zh: 但她说她并不是在一个特别政治化的家庭中长大的，但在她开始组建自己的家庭时。

sentences.en: I think that's when I really started paying attention to what was going on in our country.
sentences.zh: 我想那时我才真正开始关注我们国家正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: She finds herself paying a little more attention to politics.
sentences.zh: 她发现自己开始更多地关注政治了。

sentences.en: 9-11 happened.
sentences.zh: 9·11 事件发生了。

sentences.en: 9-11 happens.
sentences.zh: 9·11 事件发生了。

sentences.en: It's terrifying.
sentences.zh: 太可怕了。

sentences.en: The country goes through a period of time where politics sort of becomes on the front burner for people in a way that it hadn't been before.
sentences.zh: 国家经历了一段时期，政治以一种前所未有的方式成为了人们关注的焦点。

sentences.en: It opened my eyes to, OK, well, I have a say in what happens, too.
sentences.zh: 它让我大开眼界，意识到，好吧，我也对发生的事情有发言权。

sentences.en: Everybody does.
sentences.zh: 每个人都有。

sentences.en: And the more she votes and the more she looks at candidates running for office, the stronger she feels about it.
sentences.zh: 她投票越多，观察参选候选人越多，她的感受就越强烈。

sentences.en: I talked to my family about the importance of voting.
sentences.zh: 我和家人谈论过投票的重要性。

sentences.en: And one of the biggest things that a lot of my family would say to me at that time was,
sentences.zh: 当时我很多家人对我说的一句最重要的话就是：

sentences.en: It's one vote.
sentences.zh: 这只是一张选票。

sentences.en: My vote doesn't matter.
sentences.zh: 我的投票无关紧要。

sentences.en: What's one vote going to do?
sentences.zh: 一张选票能做什么？

sentences.en: And I never really tried to sway them one way or the other.
sentences.zh: 我从来没有试图说服他们支持哪一方。

sentences.en: I just said, this is important.
sentences.zh: 我只是说，这很重要。

sentences.en: Like, you should have a say in what's going on.
sentences.zh: 就像，你应该对正在发生的事情有发言权。

sentences.en: Because you can't.
sentences.zh: 因为你不能放弃。

sentences.en: She kind of becomes an evangelist for voting.
sentences.zh: 她成了一名投票的传道者。

sentences.en: And by the time 2016 happens.
sentences.zh: 到了 2016 年的时候。

sentences.en: So 2016, I voted for Trump.
sentences.zh: 所以 2016 年，我投给了特朗普。

sentences.en: Nikki finds herself very interested in Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 尼基发现自己对唐纳德·特朗普非常感兴趣。

sentences.en: I liked what he stood for.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢他的立场。

sentences.en: I did like that he was kind of an outsider to politics.
sentences.zh: 我确实喜欢他那种政治局外人的身份。

sentences.en: She admired the different approach that he brought to speaking about politics.
sentences.zh: 她钦佩他谈论政治时所带来的不同方式。

sentences.en: So Trump's elected.
sentences.zh: 所以特朗普当选了。

sentences.en: And when 2020 rolled around.
sentences.zh: 当 2020 年到来时。

sentences.en: COVID happened.
sentences.zh: 新冠疫情发生了。

sentences.en: And then all these different policies happened around voting.
sentences.zh: 然后所有这些关于投票的不同政策都出台了。

sentences.en: Wisconsin has to figure out how to put on an election when there's a pandemic happening.
sentences.zh: 威斯康星州必须想办法在疫情期间进行选举。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: If you remember back in the presidential primary in April of 2020,
sentences.zh: 如果你还记得 2020 年 4 月的总统初选，

sentences.en: Wisconsin was the first place to try to run an in-person election during the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 威斯康星州是第一个尝试在疫情期间进行现场投票的地方。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And April 2020 is literally like just a few weeks into the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 而 2020 年 4 月，实际上距离疫情爆发才仅仅几周。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And it was a disaster.
sentences.zh: 那是一场灾难。

sentences.en: The Democratic governor, Tony Evers, tried to postpone the election like they did in a few other states to try to sort of get their act together.
sentences.zh: 民主党州长托尼·埃弗斯试图像其他几个州一样推迟选举，以便让一切步入正轨。

sentences.en: The Republicans in the state legislature and the conservatives who control the state Supreme Court blocked him from doing so.
sentences.zh: 州议会的共和党人和控制州最高法院的保守派阻止了他这样做。

sentences.en: And so they held an election that wound up with almost all of the normal polling places were closed.
sentences.zh: 于是他们举行了一场选举，结果几乎所有正常的投票站都关闭了。

sentences.en: In Milwaukee, there were lines around the block, in the rain, in a pandemic.
sentences.zh: 在密尔沃基，人们在雨中排起了长队，而当时正处于疫情期间。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And it really delivered an image of incompetence in dealing with the pandemic that kind of signified like what a mess things were both in Wisconsin and the whole country.
sentences.zh: 这确实呈现出一种应对疫情无能的形象，象征着威斯康星州乃至整个国家当时是多么混乱。

sentences.en: And so because the primary was such a mess, officials in Wisconsin took a number of steps to avoid a repeat during the general election.
sentences.zh: 由于初选如此混乱，威斯康星州的官员采取了一些措施，以避免在大选中重蹈覆辙。

sentences.en: And what did those steps look like?
sentences.zh: 这些措施是什么样的？

sentences.en: Well, Michael, the thing to understand about Wisconsin elections is that they're run by 1,850 municipal clerks in every city, village, and town in the state.
sentences.zh: 嗯，迈克尔，关于威斯康星州选举，你需要了解的是，它们是由全州每个城市、村庄和城镇的 1850 名市政书记官管理的。

sentences.en: And those clerks get their guidance and rules on how to run elections from a state body called the Wisconsin Elections Commission, which everybody here just calls the WEC.
sentences.zh: 这些书记官从一个名为“威斯康星州选举委员会”（大家简称为 WEC）的州机构那里获得关于如何进行选举的指导和规则。

sentences.en: It has six members.
sentences.zh: 它有六名成员。

sentences.en: There's three Republicans and three Democrats.
sentences.zh: 三名共和党人，三名民主党人。

sentences.en: And the idea is that they are supposed to give guidance and make rules in a bipartisan fashion.
sentences.zh: 其理念是他们应该以两党合作的方式提供指导并制定规则。

sentences.en: So the commission had the job of trying to figure out how people were going to vote during the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 所以委员会的任务是设法弄清楚人们在疫情期间将如何投票。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So what did the WEC do in 2020?
sentences.zh: 那么 WEC 在 2020 年做了什么？

sentences.en: So the commission took some creative license with the state's voting laws.
sentences.zh: 委员会对该州的投票法采取了一些创造性的解释。

sentences.en: Take the state's nursing homes that were in lockdown like they were all over the country.
sentences.zh: 以该州的疗养院为例，它们像全国各地一样处于封锁状态。

sentences.en: Before the pandemic,
sentences.zh: 疫情之前，

sentences.en: people who were confined there who needed help filling out their ballots would call two special voting deputies from their local clerk's office to come in and help them with their ballots.
sentences.zh: 被困在那里需要帮助填写选票的人，会打电话给当地书记官办公室的两名特别投票代表，让他们进来协助填写。

sentences.en: But during the pandemic, deputies, like everybody else, weren't allowed inside the nursing homes.
sentences.zh: 但在疫情期间，代表们和其他人一样，不被允许进入疗养院。

sentences.en: And so the commission allowed nursing home staff to help people fill out their absentee ballots instead.
sentences.zh: 因此，委员会允许疗养院工作人员协助人们填写缺席选票。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: They changed the rules also around absentee ballots.
sentences.zh: 他们还改变了关于缺席选票的规则。

sentences.en: So before the pandemic, a Wisconsin voter would have to specifically ask for an absentee ballot application.
sentences.zh: 疫情之前，威斯康星州的选民必须专门申请缺席选票。

sentences.en: But during the pandemic, they allowed a mass mailing of absentee ballot applications to all the voters.
sentences.zh: 但在疫情期间，他们允许向所有选民大规模邮寄缺席选票申请表。

sentences.en: The third thing that they did was change the guidance on drop boxes, which really hadn't been used very much in Wisconsin before the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 他们做的第三件事是改变了关于投票箱的指导方针，这在疫情前在威斯康星州并没有被广泛使用。

sentences.en: Now the commission was allowing clerks to distribute drop boxes around their communities so people could return their ballots without having to go inside or putting them in the mail.
sentences.zh: 现在委员会允许书记官在社区周围分发投票箱，这样人们就可以归还选票，而不必进入室内或通过邮寄方式。

sentences.en: So the commission's approach was, how can we make it easier to vote and specifically make it easier to vote remotely in the middle of a pandemic?
sentences.zh: 所以委员会的方法是，我们如何才能让投票变得更容易，特别是让在疫情期间远程投票变得更容易？

sentences.en: Yeah, it was all about trying to make it easier and safer for people to vote during this period of time.
sentences.zh: 是的，这一切都是为了让人们在这段时期投票变得更容易、更安全。

sentences.en: And in a way, it worked.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，它奏效了。

sentences.en: More people in Wisconsin voted absentee in 2020 than had in any election up to that point.
sentences.zh: 2020 年威斯康星州缺席投票的人数比以往任何一次选举都要多。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯嗯。

sentences.en: But for Nikki, this all seemed kind of funny.
sentences.zh: 但对尼基来说，这一切看起来有点奇怪。

sentences.en: That's the first time I think I've really ever heard or paid attention to the whole absentee ballots.
sentences.zh: 我想这是我第一次真正听说或关注整个缺席选票的事情。

sentences.en: And...
sentences.zh: 而且……

sentences.en: You know, she'd never thought that much about absentee ballots before.
sentences.zh: 你知道，她以前从未过多考虑过缺席选票。

sentences.en: Like, is this normal?
sentences.zh: 比如，这正常吗？

sentences.en: Does this always happen?
sentences.zh: 这总是发生吗？

sentences.en: And I just never paid attention to it.
sentences.zh: 我从来没有关注过它。

sentences.en: And of course, at this time, Donald Trump is talking a lot about the ills and perils of absentee voting.
sentences.zh: 当然，当时唐纳德·特朗普正在大谈缺席投票的弊端和危险。

sentences.en: Right, and so are his supporters.
sentences.zh: 没错，他的支持者也是如此。

sentences.en: And even though the state election commission was bipartisan and Republicans on the commission supported these new changes,
sentences.zh: 尽管州选举委员会是两党组成的，而且委员会中的共和党人也支持这些新变化，

sentences.en: a lot of the Republican lawmakers in the state felt the WEC had taken things too far.
sentences.zh: 但州内许多共和党议员认为 WEC 做得太过分了。

sentences.en: Hi, Senator Bernier.
sentences.zh: 你好，伯尼尔参议员。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: It's really good to meet you.
sentences.zh: 很高兴见到你。

sentences.en: I don't know that we've met, but it's good to meet you.
sentences.zh: 我不知道我们是否见过面，但很高兴认识你。

sentences.en: And one of those who was concerned was one of the people in the state who knows the system beSt.
sentences.zh: 其中一位对此感到担忧的人，是州里最了解这套系统的人之一。

sentences.en: Give me a quick tour of your office.
sentences.zh: 带我快速参观一下你的办公室吧。

sentences.en: Like, do you have any memorabilia or anything?
sentences.zh: 比如，你这里有什么纪念品之类的东西吗？

sentences.en: A state senator named Kathy Bernier.
sentences.zh: 一位名叫凯西·伯尼尔的州参议员。

sentences.en: And then the Dairy Business Association.
sentences.zh: 还有乳制品商业协会。

sentences.en: Can you describe what that award looks like?
sentences.zh: 你能描述一下那个奖项长什么样吗？

sentences.en: Looks like a cow.
sentences.zh: 看起来像头牛。

sentences.en: Yeah, so...
sentences.zh: 是啊，所以……

sentences.en: Made of glass, right?
sentences.zh: 是玻璃做的，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, well, plastic, technically.
sentences.zh: 嗯，严格来说是塑料的。

sentences.en: Tell us about Senator Bernier.
sentences.zh: 跟我们讲讲伯尼尔参议员吧。

sentences.en: So, Kathy Bernier has spent her entire political life working on elections.
sentences.zh: 凯西·伯尼尔的整个政治生涯都致力于选举工作。

sentences.en: She got her started in 1998 when she was elected the county clerk of Chippewa County in western Wisconsin.
sentences.zh: 她始于1998年，当时她当选为威斯康星州西部奇佩瓦县的县书记官。

sentences.en: And there, she oversaw voting for a decade, helping the municipal clerks in her county run their elections.
sentences.zh: 在那里，她负责监督选举长达十年，帮助县里的市政书记官组织选举。

sentences.en: Eventually, she runs and wins a seat in the state assembly.
sentences.zh: 最终，她竞选并赢得了州众议院的一个席位。

sentences.en: I was on the election committee right away.
sentences.zh: 我一进去就加入了选举委员会。

sentences.en: And once she gets in the state legislature, she works on elections issues.
sentences.zh: 一旦进入州立法机构，她就开始处理选举问题。

sentences.en: She gets herself on the state's elections committee.
sentences.zh: 她让自己进入了州选举委员会。

sentences.en: She writes the voting laws.
sentences.zh: 她负责起草选举法。

sentences.en: She knows this inside and out.
sentences.zh: 她对这些了如指掌。

sentences.en: And so, when the pandemic hits...
sentences.zh: 所以，当疫情来袭时……

sentences.en: So, COVID put an entire new twist on the elections.
sentences.zh: 新冠疫情给选举带来了全新的变数。

sentences.en: She gets worried about what the Elections Commission is doing.
sentences.zh: 她开始担心选举委员会在做什么。

sentences.en: I had a conversation with Dean Knudsen, who sat on the Wisconsin Election Commission.
sentences.zh: 我和曾在威斯康星州选举委员会任职的迪恩·克努森谈过。

sentences.en: You know, I told him I didn't disagree with being able to use Dropboxes.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我告诉他我不反对使用投票箱。

sentences.en: But I argued with him that the law doesn't allow for it.
sentences.zh: 但我跟他争论说，法律并不允许这样做。

sentences.en: And she knows that their decisions to expand the use of Dropboxes and allow people in nursing homes to vote without special voting deputies don't fit within the state law.
sentences.zh: 她知道他们扩大使用投票箱、允许疗养院居民在没有特别投票代理人的情况下投票的决定，并不符合州法律。

sentences.en: We have no law that allows for it.
sentences.zh: 我们没有任何法律允许这样做。

sentences.en: And these things that didn't seem quite right to Nikki also weren't right to Senator Bernier because she, perhaps as much as anyone else in the state,
sentences.zh: 这些在妮基看来不太对劲的事情，在伯尼尔参议员看来也不对劲，因为她或许比州里任何人都更了解……

sentences.en: understands what the state law says and what it doesn't say.
sentences.zh: 州法律规定了什么，没规定什么。

sentences.en: So, headed into Election Day, this is the atmosphere.
sentences.zh: 所以，临近选举日，气氛就是这样。

sentences.en: Real Republican worry at lots of different levels about this new pandemic-era system of Wisconsin voting.
sentences.zh: 共和党人对威斯康星州这种疫情期间的新投票系统，在各个层面都感到真正的担忧。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so, in Racine County on Election Day, Nikki heads out to vote.
sentences.zh: 所以在选举日当天的拉辛县，妮基出发去投票了。

sentences.en: I was going to go to a place and vote.
sentences.zh: 我打算去一个地方投票。

sentences.en: I wasn't sending anything in.
sentences.zh: 我没有寄送任何东西。

sentences.en: I wasn't doing an absentee ballot.
sentences.zh: 我没有使用缺席选票。

sentences.en: Like, I wanted to go and put my vote on paper.
sentences.zh: 我想亲自去把我的选票投在纸上。

sentences.en: Put it in the machine.
sentences.zh: 放进机器里。

sentences.en: You know, there was no chance that she was going to use an absentee ballot or a Dropbox.
sentences.zh: 你知道，她根本不可能使用缺席选票或投票箱。

sentences.en: She wanted to know that her ballot was fed into the voting machine herself.
sentences.zh: 她想亲眼确认自己的选票被送进了投票机。

sentences.en: And did it feel secure to you once you did?
sentences.zh: 当你投完票后，你觉得安全吗？

sentences.en: I think I looked at things a little bit differently.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我看待事情的方式有点不同了。

sentences.en: I looked at, like, I remember looking at, like, the pen that I used, even.
sentences.zh: 我记得我甚至盯着我用的那支笔看。

sentences.en: Just looking over the ballot.
sentences.zh: 只是检查了一下选票。

sentences.en: And felt a little bit different putting it into the machine.
sentences.zh: 把它放进机器时感觉有点不一样。

sentences.en: Like, I hope this counts.
sentences.zh: 就像是，希望这票能算数。

sentences.en: So that night, at Nikki's house, her family watches the election results come in.
sentences.zh: 那天晚上，在妮基家，她的家人看着选举结果陆续出炉。

sentences.en: It is 10 o'clock here in New York City.
sentences.zh: 现在是纽约时间晚上10点。

sentences.en: Polls have just closed in another four states.
sentences.zh: 另外四个州的投票站刚刚关闭。

sentences.en: Let's start with...
sentences.zh: 让我们从……开始

sentences.en: We were all just sitting around watching it.
sentences.zh: 我们当时都坐在一起看结果。

sentences.en: Like, we will have, like, family dinner and stuff like that where they come over.
sentences.zh: 就像我们平时会有的家庭晚餐之类的，他们会过来。

sentences.en: So it was just kind of like any other night that we would have done that.
sentences.zh: 所以这就像我们平时会做的任何一个晚上一样。

sentences.en: But we were watching this.
sentences.zh: 但我们当时在看这个。

sentences.en: I'm going to interrupt you.
sentences.zh: 我要打断你一下。

sentences.en: We're going to make a big call right here.
sentences.zh: 我们现在要发布一个重大预测。

sentences.en: The Fox News decision desk can now project that President Donald Trump will win the state of Florida.
sentences.zh: 福克斯新闻决策台现在可以预测唐纳德·特朗普总统将赢得佛罗里达州。

sentences.en: 29 electoral votes.
sentences.zh: 29张选举人票。

sentences.en: And he will...
sentences.zh: 他将……

sentences.en: The way numbers were coming in, it looked like he was, you know, winning the big numbers that he needed to.
sentences.zh: 从票数统计来看，他似乎正在赢得他所需要的大量选票。

sentences.en: Fox News, the decision desk, can now call the state of Ohio for President Trump.
sentences.zh: 福克斯新闻决策台现在可以宣布特朗普总统赢得俄亥俄州。

sentences.en: You can't get to the White House.
sentences.zh: 你无法进入白宫。

sentences.en: The Republican couldn't.
sentences.zh: 共和党人做不到。

sentences.en: Without Ohio, he now wins Ohio.
sentences.zh: 没有俄亥俄州，他现在赢得了俄亥俄州。

sentences.en: We all kind of, like, we're in the mindset of he's going to win.
sentences.zh: 我们当时都觉得，他会赢。

sentences.en: Donald Trump wins if he wins Pennsylvania, if he wins Wisconsin.
sentences.zh: 如果唐纳德·特朗普赢下宾夕法尼亚州和威斯康星州，他就赢了。

sentences.en: And it's possible that he could win Wisconsin.
sentences.zh: 而且他有可能赢下威斯康星州。

sentences.en: Like, this is good.
sentences.zh: 这很好。

sentences.en: This was a good night.
sentences.zh: 这是一个美好的夜晚。

sentences.en: And that night, if you remember, Trump was winning in Wisconsin.
sentences.zh: 那天晚上，如果你还记得的话，特朗普在威斯康星州是领先的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The Election Day vote was a big Republican vote for him.
sentences.zh: 选举日的投票对他来说是巨大的共和党票仓。

sentences.en: And when I went to sleep, I can't remember the exact time, but it was later.
sentences.zh: 当我睡觉时，我不记得具体时间了，但很晚了。

sentences.en: I went to sleep because I'm like, that's good.
sentences.zh: 我去睡觉了，因为我觉得，这很好。

sentences.en: Like, he won.
sentences.zh: 他赢了。

sentences.en: But when she wakes up the next morning...
sentences.zh: 但当她第二天早上醒来时……

sentences.en: Woke up and was like, what happened?
sentences.zh: 醒来后心想，发生了什么？

sentences.en: Joe Biden is ahead in Wisconsin by a few thousand votes.
sentences.zh: 乔·拜登在威斯康星州以几千票的优势领先。

sentences.en: Democratic nominee Joe Biden appears to have a narrow lead over President Trump in the fight for those 270 electoral college votes.
sentences.zh: 民主党候选人乔·拜登在争夺那270张选举人票的竞争中，似乎对特朗普总统保持着微弱优势。

sentences.en: Now, this could all change...
sentences.zh: 现在，这一切都可能改变……

sentences.en: I was surprised.
sentences.zh: 我很惊讶。

sentences.en: Very shocked and surprised when I woke up.
sentences.zh: 醒来时非常震惊和意外。

sentences.en: Joe Biden holding a lead, 238, to President Trump's 213...
sentences.zh: 乔·拜登以238票领先特朗普总统的213票……

sentences.en: I was watching the TV and I was just, like, in kind of disbelief.
sentences.zh: 我当时看着电视，简直不敢相信。

sentences.en: It's coming down to a few key swing states, including Michigan, where Joe Biden has a slight lead, and Wisconsin, where Joe Biden is also with a slight lead...
sentences.zh: 结果取决于几个关键的摇摆州，包括密歇根州，乔·拜登在那里有微弱优势，还有威斯康星州，乔·拜登在那里也有微弱优势……

sentences.en: And then I just remember, you know, then more details coming out about how, you know, a bunch of votes came in in the middle of the night.
sentences.zh: 然后我只记得，后来有更多细节传出，关于半夜里涌入了大量选票。

sentences.en: And, like, that was weird.
sentences.zh: 这很奇怪。

sentences.en: What happened was, and I remember because I stayed up for this, at about 3 in the morning, a big tranche of absentee ballots were reported.
sentences.zh: 发生的事情是——我记得很清楚，因为我熬夜等结果——凌晨3点左右，一大批缺席选票被报告出来。

sentences.en: And those ballots were primarily Democratic, and they put Joe Biden into the lead in Wisconsin.
sentences.zh: 这些选票主要是民主党的，它们让乔·拜登在威斯康星州取得了领先。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so, when Nikki and the rest of the state woke up in the morning, they found that what they, when they went to bed, was a Trump advantage, was now a Joe Biden lead.
sentences.zh: 所以，当妮基和州里其他人早上醒来时，他们发现睡觉前特朗普的优势，现在变成了乔·拜登的领先。

sentences.en: So, for Nikki, it didn't add up.
sentences.zh: 对妮基来说，这说不通。

sentences.en: And it was suspicious, and it seemed fishy.
sentences.zh: 这很可疑，看起来有猫腻。

sentences.en: But for others, particularly people who knew how elections worked inside and out, like Senator Bernier, it made a lot of sense.
sentences.zh: 但对其他人，特别是像伯尼尔参议员这样对选举运作了如指掌的人来说，这很有道理。

sentences.en: So, the fact that it takes a long time for large cities to count their ballots, especially when there are so many absentee ballots, is not surprising to me.
sentences.zh: 所以，大城市统计选票需要很长时间，尤其是在有这么多缺席选票的情况下，我一点也不感到惊讶。

sentences.en: A Republican has to be thousands of votes ahead before Milwaukee finishes counting, because you are going to lose your lead without question.
sentences.zh: 共和党人必须在密尔沃基完成计票前领先数千票，因为毫无疑问，你会失去领先优势。

sentences.en: Because even before 2020, the big Democratic cities in Wisconsin tended to take longer to count their votes than smaller Republican districts.
sentences.zh: 因为即使在2020年之前，威斯康星州的大型民主党城市统计选票的速度往往就比小型共和党地区要慢。

sentences.en: And the Republican votes would get tallied firSt.
sentences.zh: 共和党的选票会先被统计出来。

sentences.en: They'd create a portrait of the results that didn't quite fit with the final reality.
sentences.zh: 它们描绘出的结果图景与最终现实并不完全吻合。

sentences.en: I knew there was going to be questions or problems, you know, with how things were carried out.
sentences.zh: 我知道事情的执行方式会有疑问或问题。

sentences.en: But I was still, I was confident in the results, and they were as accurate as they possibly can be.
sentences.zh: 但我仍然对结果充满信心，它们尽可能地准确。

sentences.en: And so, this is where Senator Bernier's experience of 2020 starts to diverge from Nikki's.
sentences.zh: 这就是伯尼尔参议员对2020年的经历开始与妮基产生分歧的地方。

sentences.en: Once in a while, there's a mistake.
sentences.zh: 偶尔会有错误。

sentences.en: Once in a while, somebody screws up.
sentences.zh: 偶尔会有人搞砸。

sentences.en: But for the most part, we have all of the checks and balances in place, so that the results are the results.
sentences.zh: 但在大多数情况下，我们所有的制衡机制都到位了，所以结果就是结果。

sentences.en: Are there people that we have caught cheating?
sentences.zh: 我们抓到过作弊的人吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, there are some.
sentences.zh: 有，确实有一些。

sentences.en: Are there some that we might not have caught?
sentences.zh: 有没有我们可能没抓到的？

sentences.en: Yep, I am sure there are some.
sentences.zh: 是的，我肯定有。

sentences.en: But not 21,000.
sentences.zh: 但绝不是21000张。

sentences.en: Ultimately, Senator Bernier had faith in the final results that came from Wisconsin, that Joe Biden won the state by just over 20,000 votes.
sentences.zh: 最终，伯尼尔参议员相信威斯康星州的最终结果，即乔·拜登以超过2万票的优势赢得了该州。

sentences.en: And she knew that the questions that she had about absentee voting were an order of magnitude too small to change the final result.
sentences.zh: 她知道她对缺席投票的质疑，在改变最终结果的量级上微不足道。

sentences.en: And she trusted that the local clerks in the state had done their job right.
sentences.zh: 她相信州里的地方书记官们已经尽职尽责。

sentences.en: And she was savvy enough to know that people who weren't in government, who didn't have her level of access, and didn't know the system well, might not believe in that result.
sentences.zh: 她足够精明，知道那些不在政府部门工作、没有她这种接触渠道、也不了解系统的人，可能不会相信这个结果。

sentences.en: My concern was, and is, that, you know, perception is important too.
sentences.zh: 我当时和现在的担忧都是，感知也很重要。

sentences.en: That you want to make sure that all of the voters have confidence in the electoral system.
sentences.zh: 你希望确保所有选民对选举制度都有信心。

sentences.en: Right, so she doesn't necessarily know Nikki, but she understands why someone like Nikki is seeing this all as so suspicious.
sentences.zh: 没错，所以她不一定认识妮基，但她理解为什么像妮基这样的人会觉得这一切如此可疑。

sentences.en: She knows a lot of people like Nikki who had doubts about the election and what had happened before and on Election Day.
sentences.zh: 她认识很多像妮基这样的人，他们对选举以及选举前和选举日发生的事情存有疑虑。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And those doubts got amplified when...
sentences.zh: 而这些疑虑在……时被放大了。

sentences.en: Fighting for truth, justice, and the American way.
sentences.zh: 为真理、正义和美国方式而战。

sentences.en: The conservative talk radio hosts in Wisconsin, who are very powerful, begin spreading allegations about what had happened.
sentences.zh: 威斯康星州那些非常有影响力的保守派脱口秀主持人开始散布关于所发生之事的指控。

sentences.en: I personally think, and again, we have to get the investigation to see there, that we have seen voter fraud on a mass scale across this country,
sentences.zh: 我个人认为，再说一次，我们必须通过调查来看看，我们已经在全国范围内看到了大规模的选民欺诈，

sentences.en: unlike anything we've ever seen before.
sentences.zh: 这是我们从未见过的。

sentences.en: And that quickly reached Nikki.
sentences.zh: 这很快传到了妮基那里。

sentences.en: You know, the things I was hearing was that there was a lot of things going on in Madison that, and I'm going to forget what they were called,
sentences.zh: 你知道，我听到的是麦迪逊发生了很多事情，我忘了它们叫什么了，

sentences.en: but they were like set up in the park and collecting votes from people.
sentences.zh: 但它们就像是在公园里设置点，收集人们的选票。

sentences.en: The same exact thing happened in Georgia, where they had RVs going through mostly minority cities and towns.
sentences.zh: 佐治亚州也发生了完全一样的事情，他们有房车穿过少数族裔聚居的城市和城镇。

sentences.en: Oh, they had an RV.
sentences.zh: 哦，他们有一辆房车。

sentences.en: Oh, they did.
sentences.zh: 哦，确实有。

sentences.en: Like, we've called it the Scooby-Doo voting machine, that they're just sort of rolling around with five teenagers and a dog.
sentences.zh: 我们把它称为史酷比投票机，他们就像带着五个青少年和一条狗到处转悠。

sentences.en: I mean, and you have...
sentences.zh: 我是说，你有……

sentences.en: I heard about the, on Dan O'Donnell, he called it like the Scooby-Mobile, but that was like going around collecting votes.
sentences.zh: 我听丹·奥唐奈说过，他称之为史酷比移动车，就是到处收集选票。

sentences.en: I've done significant research and significant reporting into the issue of nursing home vote fraud in Wisconsin.
sentences.zh: 我对威斯康星州疗养院选票欺诈的问题进行了深入的研究和报道。

sentences.en: And then in the nursing homes, they were collecting a ton of votes from people in the nursing homes.
sentences.zh: 然后在疗养院里，他们从疗养院的人那里收集了大量的选票。

sentences.en: You actually had nursing home staff members filling out ballots.
sentences.zh: 你实际上有疗养院的工作人员在填写选票。

sentences.en: To my knowledge, this is what happened.
sentences.zh: 据我所知，事情就是这样发生的。

sentences.en: They either filled out ballots or someone who is clearly not mentally able to vote.
sentences.zh: 他们要么代填选票，要么就是针对那些显然没有投票能力的人。

sentences.en: They were saying, oh, do you want to vote for Joe Biden?
sentences.zh: 他们会说，哦，你想投乔·拜登吗？

sentences.en: They wouldn't respond.
sentences.zh: 他们不会回应。

sentences.en: They'd say, okay, we're voting for Joe Biden.
sentences.zh: 他们就会说，好的，我们投给乔·拜登。

sentences.en: And there were some, you know, certain stories I heard on different podcasts or on the radio, just about, you know, people's parents, you know, voted and they never voted before.
sentences.zh: 我还在不同的播客或广播里听到过一些故事，关于人们的父母，他们以前从没投过票。

sentences.en: Or, you know, like, they can't even know, they don't even know what day it is.
sentences.zh: 或者，他们甚至不知道今天是什么日子。

sentences.en: But they voted for the president.
sentences.zh: 但他们投了总统的票。

sentences.en: And with everything she heard, Nikki was feeling more and more frustrated about the election.
sentences.zh: 随着她听到的一切，妮基对选举感到越来越沮丧。

sentences.en: I kept following those stories as things progressed.
sentences.zh: 随着事情的发展，我一直在关注那些报道。

sentences.en: And my biggest thing is, why aren't we doing anything about this?
sentences.zh: 我最关心的是，为什么我们对此什么都不做？

sentences.en: Why isn't this getting, you know, more attention?
sentences.zh: 为什么这没有得到更多的关注？

sentences.en: I definitely talked a lot about it to my husband.
sentences.zh: 我确实和我的丈夫谈过很多次这件事。

sentences.en: And he just, you know, what are you going to do, Nikki?
sentences.zh: 他只是说，你知道的，尼基，你打算怎么办呢？

sentences.en: And I'm like, well, I don't know, but something needs to happen.
sentences.zh: 我说，我不知道，但必须得做点什么。

sentences.en: Like, more people need to question things instead of just being complacent with the answer they're given.
sentences.zh: 比如，人们需要更多地质疑现状，而不是对被告知的答案盲目顺从。

sentences.en: And then Donald Trump himself comes out and says,
sentences.zh: 然后唐纳德·特朗普本人出来说，

sentences.en: Well, actually, I won Wisconsin.
sentences.zh: 其实，我赢了威斯康星州。

sentences.en: Wisconsin was stolen from me.
sentences.zh: 威斯康星州是从我手中偷走的。

sentences.en: But I actually won.
sentences.zh: 但我实际上赢了。

sentences.en: And this was not what Senator Bernier wanted to hear.
sentences.zh: 而这并不是伯尼尔参议员想听到的。

sentences.en: So when Trump came out in December and said, actually, I won Wisconsin, what went through your mind?
sentences.zh: 所以当特朗普在十二月出来说，实际上我赢了威斯康星州时，你脑子里在想什么？

sentences.en: And what did you think his supporters in Wisconsin would think about that?
sentences.zh: 你认为他在威斯康星州的支持者会怎么想？

sentences.en: Grr.
sentences.zh: 呃。

sentences.en: Because she knows this will give ammunition to Donald Trump supporters in the state who had any doubts about the results.
sentences.zh: 因为她知道这会给州内那些对选举结果有疑虑的唐纳德·特朗普支持者提供弹药。

sentences.en: But Trump doesn't stop there.
sentences.zh: 但特朗普并没有就此罢休。

sentences.en: He starts calling out the Republican leaders in Wisconsin, saying they were deliberately covering up election fraud.
sentences.zh: 他开始点名批评威斯康星州的共和党领导人，称他们蓄意掩盖选举舞弊。

sentences.en: And eventually, the pressure becomes so intense that some of these lawmakers give in.
sentences.zh: 最终，压力变得如此巨大，以至于一些议员屈服了。

sentences.en: The Republican Speaker of the State Assembly authorizes an investigation to look into election fraud, not led by an independent investigator,
sentences.zh: 州众议院的共和党议长授权进行一项调查以查明选举舞弊，调查并非由独立调查员领导，

sentences.en: but by a highly partisan former state Supreme Court justice who already had claimed the election was stolen from Trump.
sentences.zh: 而是由一位立场极度偏颇的前州最高法院法官领导，他此前已经声称选举是从特朗普手中偷走的。

sentences.en: And that caught Senator Bernier off guard.
sentences.zh: 这让伯尼尔参议员措手不及。

sentences.en: I thought, that's not the plan.
sentences.zh: 我想，这不是计划好的。

sentences.en: I had a discussion about the plan.
sentences.zh: 我曾讨论过这个计划。

sentences.en: Because in her mind, the way to handle election doubts was to calmly explain to people what had happened.
sentences.zh: 因为在她看来，处理选举疑虑的方法是冷静地向人们解释发生了什么。

sentences.en: The plan was to educate the electorate on the election system here in the state of Wisconsin, to start turning the ship,
sentences.zh: 计划是向威斯康星州的选民普及选举制度，开始扭转局面，

sentences.en: and to get everyone to cool their jets a little bit and wait for them.
sentences.zh: 让大家稍微冷静一下，等待结果。

sentences.en: She met with constituents.
sentences.zh: 她会见了选民。

sentences.en: She told them the election wasn't stolen.
sentences.zh: 她告诉他们选举没有被窃取。

sentences.en: She explained why the election results started in Trump's favor and switched to Biden.
sentences.zh: 她解释了为什么选举结果起初对特朗普有利，后来转为对拜登有利。

sentences.en: And to her, this partisan investigation became sort of a theater of the absurd.
sentences.zh: 对她来说，这场党派调查变成了一场荒诞剧。

sentences.en: It drags on for months.
sentences.zh: 它拖了好几个月。

sentences.en: It costs more than a million dollars.
sentences.zh: 它花费了超过一百万美元。

sentences.en: The investigator tried to subpoena local officials.
sentences.zh: 调查员试图传唤当地官员。

sentences.en: He threatened to put them in jail for not talking to them.
sentences.zh: 他威胁说如果他们不配合就将他们关进监狱。

sentences.en: He takes meetings with well-known conspiracy theorists.
sentences.zh: 他与知名的阴谋论者会面。

sentences.en: And eventually, Senator Bernier decided she'd had enough.
sentences.zh: 最终，伯尼尔参议员决定受够了。

sentences.en: It's a pleasure to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: In December of 2021, she goes to a press conference and she says...
sentences.zh: 2021年12月，她参加了一场新闻发布会，她说……

sentences.en: This is a charade, what's going on, with this constant drumbeat of all the massive voter fraud and nobody...
sentences.zh: 这是一场闹剧，正在发生的事情，不断鼓吹大规模选民舞弊，而没有人……

sentences.en: This investigation is a sham.
sentences.zh: 这项调查是虚假的。

sentences.en: There's a simple explanation for almost every single thing that people accuse election officials of doing.
sentences.zh: 人们指责选举官员所做的每一件事，几乎都有一个简单的解释。

sentences.en: There's an explanation for almost all of it.
sentences.zh: 几乎所有事情都有解释。

sentences.en: And so I think the Gableman investigation should come to a close sooner rather than later.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为盖布尔曼的调查应该尽早结束。

sentences.en: You know, she felt like the partisan investigator had been totally out of control with his investigation.
sentences.zh: 你知道，她觉得那位党派调查员的调查完全失控了。

sentences.en: Because the longer we keep this up, the more harm we're going to do for Republicans.
sentences.zh: 因为我们维持的时间越长，对共和党造成的伤害就越大。

sentences.en: And I'm doing this for herself.
sentences.zh: 我这样做是为了她自己。

sentences.en: And she says, I'm a Republican.
sentences.zh: 她说，我是共和党人。

sentences.en: When Benjamin Franklin came out of the convention and our Constitution was created, he was asked, what kind of government do we have?
sentences.zh: 当本杰明·富兰克林走出制宪会议，我们的宪法制定出来时，有人问他，我们拥有什么样的政府？

sentences.en: And he said, a republic, if we can keep it.
sentences.zh: 他说，一个共和国，如果我们能保住它的话。

sentences.en: We're in jeopardy of losing it.
sentences.zh: 我们正面临失去它的危险。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Thank you so much, Senator Bernier.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢，伯尼尔参议员。

sentences.en: Why did you decide to do that?
sentences.zh: 你为什么决定这样做？

sentences.en: Because our election officials were getting beat up as if they did something fraudulent in the electoral process to give Joe Biden an edge.
sentences.zh: 因为我们的选举官员受到了攻击，好像他们在选举过程中做了什么欺诈行为来给乔·拜登优势一样。

sentences.en: And I just knew that not to be true.
sentences.zh: 但我知道那不是真的。

sentences.en: But despite Kathy's plea, the investigation continues.
sentences.zh: 但尽管凯西恳求，调查仍在继续。

sentences.en: The investigator eventually published a report in which he suggests that the state legislature should seek to decertify Joe Biden's election in Wisconsin.
sentences.zh: 调查员最终发布了一份报告，建议州议会寻求撤销乔·拜登在威斯康星州的选举结果。

sentences.en: Which, of course, is something that's not possible.
sentences.zh: 当然，这是不可能的。

sentences.en: There's no mechanism to do that.
sentences.zh: 没有机制可以做到这一点。

sentences.en: But once the report's out there, it's like pouring gasoline on the fire of Wisconsin Republicans who think that there's a way to undo the 2020 election.
sentences.zh: 但报告一出，就像给那些认为有办法推翻2020年选举的威斯康星州共和党人的火上浇油。

sentences.en: So among Republicans in Wisconsin, voices like Senator Bernier's are just being overwhelmed by people who want something done about this election fraud they believe took place.
sentences.zh: 因此，在威斯康星州的共和党人中，像伯尼尔参议员这样的声音正被那些想要解决他们认为发生的选举舞弊的人所淹没。

sentences.en: Something big and decisive.
sentences.zh: 一些重大且果断的行动。

sentences.en: And that's what happens.
sentences.zh: 事情就是这样发生的。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯 DealBook 报道商业和政策。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市的 DealBook 峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最有影响力的领导人，包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼等等。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无保留、未经修饰的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at NYTimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 我们将在11月18日通过 NYTimes.com 为所有人免费直播精选采访。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序观看，并获得一个月的免费访问权限，阅读我们所有的报道。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你不会想错过的。

sentences.en: Sir Reid, you said that in the aftermath of the 2020 election, voices from within the Republican base are demanding tangible changes to the Wisconsin election system.
sentences.zh: 里德先生，你说过在2020年大选之后，共和党基层的声音要求对威斯康星州的选举制度进行实质性改变。

sentences.en: So what do Republican leaders end up actually doing in response to those demands?
sentences.zh: 那么共和党领导人最终采取了什么行动来回应这些要求？

sentences.en: Michael, they start what becomes an all-out assault on the state's election system.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，他们发动了一场针对该州选举制度的全面攻击。

sentences.en: It begins with a right-wing activist group that brings a lawsuit seeking to end the use of drop boxes in Wisconsin.
sentences.zh: 它始于一个右翼激进组织提起诉讼，寻求结束在威斯康星州使用投票箱。

sentences.en: The case eventually goes to the state Supreme Court, which has a four-to-three conservative majority, and they rule that just about all drop boxes are illegal.
sentences.zh: 案件最终上诉至州最高法院，该法院有四比三的保守派多数，他们裁定几乎所有的投票箱都是非法的。

sentences.en: It's a big ruling.
sentences.zh: 这是一个重大的裁决。

sentences.en: It's a big ruling.
sentences.zh: 这是一个重大的裁决。

sentences.en: But where things really kick into high gear is in the state legislature, where Republicans in both chambers begin trying to rewrite the state's election laws.
sentences.zh: 但真正进入高潮的是在州议会，两院的共和党人开始试图重写该州的选举法。

sentences.en: My colleagues want to draft all kinds of bills to deal with election fraud and election issues.
sentences.zh: 我的同事们想草拟各种法案来处理选举舞弊和选举问题。

sentences.en: And once again, Senator Kathy Bernier is at the middle of this.
sentences.zh: 而凯西·伯尼尔参议员再次处于这场风暴的中心。

sentences.en: We had people on our side of the aisle, our constituents out there screaming and wailing and whatever, and they wanted to appease them.
sentences.zh: 我们党内有人，我们的选民在外面尖叫、哀号等等，他们想安抚他们。

sentences.en: As it happens, she is the chairwoman of the Senate committee that deals with elections.
sentences.zh: 碰巧，她是负责选举的参议院委员会主席。

sentences.en: She's really the gatekeeper for any election laws in the state of Wisconsin.
sentences.zh: 她实际上是威斯康星州任何选举法的把关人。

sentences.en: So they're drafting bills like crazy.
sentences.zh: 所以他们疯狂地起草法案。

sentences.en: And she's just being inundated...
sentences.zh: 而她正被淹没在……

sentences.en: Numerous bills.
sentences.zh: 无数的法案。

sentences.en: ...with proposals from her conservative colleagues.
sentences.zh: ……来自她保守派同事的提案中。

sentences.en: My staff will tell you I'm very fussy when I draft legislation or accept it in my committee.
sentences.zh: 我的员工会告诉你，我在起草立法或在我的委员会接受立法时非常挑剔。

sentences.en: It has to be drafted precisely right, or I won't accept it.
sentences.zh: 它必须起草得非常准确，否则我不会接受。

sentences.en: And she says that those colleagues were in such a rush to pass new election bills that some of these proposals were a mess.
sentences.zh: 她说，那些同事急于通过新的选举法案，以至于其中一些提案一团糟。

sentences.en: Many of the drafts were sloppy, and I wasn't going to accept just any piece of legislation.
sentences.zh: 许多草案都很草率，我不会接受任何随意的立法。

sentences.en: And of course, when I wouldn't do it, I had a colleague send out a press release chastising me.
sentences.zh: 当然，当我拒绝这样做时，我的一位同事发了一份新闻稿来斥责我。

sentences.en: And so that is where a lot of Trump supporters felt that I was hindering things.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是许多特朗普支持者认为我在阻碍事情的地方。

sentences.en: I wasn't hindering anything.
sentences.zh: 我没有阻碍任何事情。

sentences.en: I just wanted to make sure that our reaction was appropriate for the situation.
sentences.zh: 我只是想确保我们的反应对局势来说是恰当的。

sentences.en: So she tries to pump the brakes, sort out what's reasonable and what's not, and stop some of the more what she saw as ridiculous proposals from getting through.
sentences.zh: 所以她试图踩刹车，理清什么是合理的，什么是不合理的，并阻止一些她认为更荒谬的提案通过。

sentences.en: But she is a Republican.
sentences.zh: 但她是一位共和党人。

sentences.en: She is a conservative Republican.
sentences.zh: 她是一位保守派共和党人。

sentences.en: And so she signs off on a number of bills, about a dozen of them passed the legislature.
sentences.zh: 所以她签署了一些法案，大约有十几项法案在议会获得通过。

sentences.en: And what do those dozen bills do?
sentences.zh: 那十几项法案做了什么？

sentences.en: Well, if you remember in 2020, the Wisconsin Elections Commission mass-mailed absentee ballot applications.
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果你还记得2020年，威斯康星州选举委员会大规模邮寄了缺席选票申请。

sentences.en: One of the bills would require voters to make a formal request for an absentee ballot and show a valid ID every election to get their ballot.
sentences.zh: 其中一项法案要求选民在每次选举时正式申请缺席选票，并出示有效身份证件才能获得选票。

sentences.en: Another bill would forbid clerks from doing something that they've always done,
sentences.zh: 另一项法案将禁止职员做他们一直做的事情，

sentences.en: which is fill in missing information like a zip code or a line on the address on the envelope that the absentee ballot is returned in.
sentences.zh: 那就是填写缺失的信息，比如缺席选票寄回信封上的邮政编码或地址行。

sentences.en: That would be illegal.
sentences.zh: 那将是非法的。

sentences.en: And if the information isn't all properly filled in, the ballot would be invalid.
sentences.zh: 如果信息没有全部正确填写，选票将无效。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 有趣。

sentences.en: So these changes are going to make absentee voting just a little bit harder.
sentences.zh: 所以这些变化会让缺席投票变得稍微困难一些。

sentences.en: Or make it hard to finish absentee voting.
sentences.zh: 或者让完成缺席投票变得困难。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And we know that Democrats are more likely to use absentee ballots than Republicans.
sentences.zh: 我们知道民主党人比共和党人更有可能使用缺席选票。

sentences.en: And so there is a real sort of partisan advantage that Republicans are seeking through these new laws.
sentences.zh: 所以共和党人通过这些新法律确实是在寻求某种党派优势。

sentences.en: And it's similar to what Republicans have been doing since 2020 and a lot of other states where they control the legislation process.
sentences.zh: 这类似于共和党自2020年以来在许多其他他们控制立法进程的州所做的事情。

sentences.en: But what's different in Wisconsin and why we're talking about Wisconsin and not anywhere else is that Republicans here are also trying to change who is in charge of elections in the state.
sentences.zh: 但威斯康星州的不同之处，以及为什么我们谈论的是威斯康星州而不是其他地方，是因为这里的共和党人也试图改变谁负责该州的选举。

sentences.en: Explain that.
sentences.zh: 解释一下。

sentences.en: What do you mean?
sentences.zh: 你是什么意思？

sentences.en: Well, if you remember, we talked about the Wisconsin Elections Commission.
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果你还记得，我们谈到了威斯康星州选举委员会。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: The legislature is trying to cut the legs out from the commission,
sentences.zh: 议会正试图削弱该委员会的权力，

sentences.en: which they allege set these policies around the pandemic that opened the system to fraud that cost Donald Trump a victory in the state.
sentences.zh: 他们声称该委员会在疫情期间制定了这些政策，使系统容易受到欺诈，导致唐纳德·特朗普在该州失利。

sentences.en: And how are they trying to cut the legs out from under the commission?
sentences.zh: 他们是如何试图削弱委员会的权力的？

sentences.en: Well, one of the things that they passed would give the legislature control over guidance that the commission hands down to the clerks.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们通过的一件事将赋予议会控制权，以管理委员会下发给职员的指导方针。

sentences.en: So you can imagine like a chain of command of state senators telling the commission what to do and the commission then handing that to the local clerks about what election rules to follow.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以想象一个指挥链，州参议员告诉委员会该做什么，然后委员会再把这些告诉当地职员应该遵循什么选举规则。

sentences.en: So basically, the Republican-controlled legislature would supplant the judgments of this commission.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，共和党控制的议会将取代该委员会的判断。

sentences.en: It would take it over.
sentences.zh: 它将接管它。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: They wouldn't be able to, you know, send a press release or any sort of guidance without the legislature say so.
sentences.zh: 他们将无法，你知道，在没有议会同意的情况下发布新闻稿或任何形式的指导。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: But there's a bigger idea out there that a lot of Republicans have embraced in the last year, which is to eliminate the commission altogether.
sentences.zh: 但还有一个更大的想法，许多共和党人在过去一年中接受了，那就是彻底取消该委员会。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And if that happens, it's not entirely clear what would take its place.
sentences.zh: 如果发生这种情况，完全不清楚什么会取代它。

sentences.en: But we know that the Republicans in the legislature are not about to hand control over the elections to any office that's run by a Democrat.
sentences.zh: 但我们知道议会中的共和党人绝不会把选举控制权交给任何由民主党人管理的办公室。

sentences.en: And so if Republicans win the elections for attorney general or secretary of state, there's been talk that election authority could be handed to one of those offices.
sentences.zh: 所以如果共和党人赢得了总检察长或州务卿的选举，有传言称选举权可能会移交给其中一个办公室。

sentences.en: They could create a new office and put a Republican in charge.
sentences.zh: 他们可以创建一个新的办公室并任命一名共和党人负责。

sentences.en: Or the legislature could keep authority for running the elections for themselves, which is something that Senator Bernier is pretty uncomfortable with.
sentences.zh: 或者议会可以自己保留管理选举的权力，这是伯尼尔参议员非常不舒服的事情。

sentences.en: Well, first of all, the legislature is a lawmaking body.
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先，议会是一个立法机构。

sentences.en: We really cannot be the executive branch and the legislative branch.
sentences.zh: 我们真的不能既是行政部门又是立法部门。

sentences.en: So I don't see that working at all.
sentences.zh: 所以我根本看不出这行得通。

sentences.en: Because to her, it would mean the legislature is the judge, jury, and executioner for how elections are run in the state,
sentences.zh: 因为对她来说，这意味着议会是该州选举如何进行的法官、陪审团和执行者，

sentences.en: even though the legislators are on the ballot themselves in a lot of these races.
sentences.zh: 尽管议员们自己在许多这些竞选中也是候选人。

sentences.en: And what's going to happen when we're in the heat of an election and there is a controversy involving a Wisconsin legislator, either in the Senate or the Assembly,
sentences.zh: 当我们处于选举热潮中，并且涉及威斯康星州议员（无论是参议院还是众议院）的争议时，会发生什么？

sentences.en: and here we've got to oversee our own decisions involving something in our own election.
sentences.zh: 在这里我们必须监督我们自己涉及我们自己选举的决定。

sentences.en: It's incompatible.
sentences.zh: 这是不兼容的。

sentences.en: We need a body to facilitate running an election one way or the other.
sentences.zh: 我们需要一个机构来促进以某种方式进行选举。

sentences.en: And Reid, what is the likelihood that the scenario that you are describing here will actually happen?
sentences.zh: 里德，你在这里描述的情况真正发生的可能性有多大？

sentences.en: Well, that's part of the reason why today's elections in Wisconsin are so consequential.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这就是为什么今天威斯康星州的选举如此重要的部分原因。

sentences.en: In the race for governor, the Democratic incumbent, Tony Evers, has been the thing holding back these Republican bills from becoming law.
sentences.zh: 在州长竞选中，民主党现任州长托尼·埃弗斯一直是阻止这些共和党法案成为法律的力量。

sentences.en: He's vetoed every bill the Republican legislature has sent him to change the way Wisconsin votes.
sentences.zh: 他否决了共和党议会送给他的每一项改变威斯康星州投票方式的法案。

sentences.en: He's actually prevented all those things we talked about from becoming law.
sentences.zh: 他实际上阻止了我们谈论的所有那些事情成为法律。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And he said he would continue to veto Republicans' efforts to change voting laws in Wisconsin or alter or eliminate the state elections commission.
sentences.zh: 他说过，他会继续否决共和党人试图改变威斯康星州选举法，或者改动、废除州选举委员会的努力。

sentences.en: But his Republican opponent, Tim Michaels, has essentially said he supports changing or eliminating the elections commission to effectively put it under Republican control.
sentences.zh: 但他的共和党对手蒂姆·迈克尔斯（Tim Michaels）基本上表示，他支持改变或废除选举委员会，从而有效地将其置于共和党的控制之下。

sentences.en: And as of this past weekend, the polls were showing the race in Wisconsin is tied.
sentences.zh: 截至上周末，民调显示威斯康星州的选情不相上下。

sentences.en: So if Michaels wins, there's really nothing to stop Wisconsin's Republican legislators from running elections exactly how they want.
sentences.zh: 所以如果迈克尔斯获胜，威斯康星州的共和党议员们就真的没有什么阻碍，可以完全按照他们想要的方式来操办选举了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I'm thinking back to that quote, Reid, you mentioned earlier from this Republican candidate saying that if he wins the governorship,
sentences.zh: 我回想起里德（Reid）你之前提到的那位共和党候选人的话，他说如果他赢得了州长职位，

sentences.en: Republicans will never lose another election in Wisconsin.
sentences.zh: 共和党人在威斯康星州就再也不会输掉任何一场选举了。

sentences.en: It sounds like what he means is things like abolishing this election commission ensures that he and the Republicans in the legislature have the power to make that statement true.
sentences.zh: 听起来他的意思是，废除这个选举委员会之类的事情，能确保他和立法机构中的共和党人有权让那句话成为现实。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, he's not wrong that he could change things to ensure that Republicans don't lose an election again if he's elected governor.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我的意思是，如果他当选州长，他确实可以通过改变一些规则来确保共和党人不再输掉选举，他这么说并没有错。

sentences.en: But even if Tim Michaels loses,
sentences.zh: 但即使蒂姆·迈克尔斯输了，

sentences.en: Republicans have drawn themselves such an efficient and aggressive gerrymander that they need to flip just a handful of legislative seats in today's elections to give themselves veto-proof supermajorities in the state legislature.
sentences.zh: 共和党人也已经为自己划定了如此高效且激进的选区重划方案，他们只需要在今天的选举中翻转少数几个立法席位，就能在州议会中获得足以推翻否决权的绝对多数席位。

sentences.en: And then they can do all of these things we're talking about regardless of who the governor is.
sentences.zh: 到那时，无论谁当州长，他们都能做我们刚才谈到的所有那些事情。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And regardless of the fact that Wisconsin remains a purple state.
sentences.zh: 而且不管威斯康星州仍然是一个摇摆州的事实如何。

sentences.en: So you're saying Republicans have two ways to make sure that they take over the state's electoral process.
sentences.zh: 所以你的意思是，共和党人有两种方式来确保他们接管该州的选举程序。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I don't think we have the proper imagination to consider what they would do with full control of the election system.
sentences.zh: 我不认为我们有足够的想象力去考虑他们一旦完全控制了选举系统会做出什么事来。

sentences.en: They will be able to do whatever they want when it comes to elections and frankly, anything else in the state.
sentences.zh: 在选举方面，他们将能够随心所欲，坦白说，在州内的任何其他事情上也是如此。

sentences.en: So given all of that, I wonder how Senator Bernier is thinking about this moment.
sentences.zh: 鉴于这一切，我想知道伯尼尔（Bernier）参议员是如何看待这一时刻的。

sentences.en: Because the forces that she in that news conference called out as excessive and that she's been trying to rein in, they are clearly prevailing.
sentences.zh: 因为她在新闻发布会上指出的那些过激势力，以及她一直试图加以约束的力量，显然正在占据上风。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Well, Senator Bernier decided not to run for re-election.
sentences.zh: 嗯，伯尼尔参议员决定不再竞选连任。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So her role as a gatekeeper is going to end.
sentences.zh: 所以她作为把关人的角色即将结束。

sentences.en: I think I've impressed upon my colleagues the importance of well-thought-out election law.
sentences.zh: 我想我已经让我的同事们意识到深思熟虑的选举法的重要性了。

sentences.en: And I'm hoping that they don't get too carried away and to be too restrictive.
sentences.zh: 我希望他们不要做得太过火，不要过于严苛。

sentences.en: There might be one or two of my colleagues that want to be incredibly restrictive.
sentences.zh: 可能有一两个同事想要采取极其严苛的手段。

sentences.en: But I think once we get through this fall election, they'll maybe realize that the majority of the system works pretty well.
sentences.zh: 但我认为一旦我们度过了这次秋季选举，他们或许会意识到这个系统的大部分运作得相当不错。

sentences.en: But she really believes that over time, a lot of this stuff is going to self-correct.
sentences.zh: 但她确实相信，随着时间的推移，很多这类事情会自我修正。

sentences.en: This too shall pass.
sentences.zh: 这一切终将过去。

sentences.en: Calling into question the electoral process is not new.
sentences.zh: 质疑选举程序并不是什么新鲜事。

sentences.en: You know, in 2000, Gore-Bush, that whole legitimacy of that president was called into question.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在2000年戈尔对阵布什的选举中，那位总统的整个合法性都受到了质疑。

sentences.en: So I don't think it's the end of this.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这还没完。

sentences.en: I think it will rear its ugly head, especially in close elections, but it definitely made us examine our processes and make sure that we're, you know,
sentences.zh: 我认为它会再次抬头，尤其是在选情胶着的时候，但这绝对促使我们审视了自己的流程，并确保我们，你知道，

sentences.en: everybody's following the same rules and we'll get through this.
sentences.zh: 每个人都遵循同样的规则，我们会度过难关的。

sentences.en: And is there a solution to all of this that you see?
sentences.zh: 那么你认为这一切有解决办法吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, just time and we have many of those naysayers and criticizers of the electoral system now working the polls.
sentences.zh: 有，只需要时间。我们现在有很多选举系统的反对者和批评者正在参与投票站的工作。

sentences.en: So they're at the polls, they're working, they're seeing the process.
sentences.zh: 所以他们就在投票站，他们在工作，他们在观察这个过程。

sentences.en: They're also witnessing that it's pretty hard to hack into the system or be fraudulent in any way.
sentences.zh: 他们也亲眼见证了黑进系统或以任何方式进行欺诈是相当困难的。

sentences.en: They also really have to deep down, if they're smart, realize that all of the things that they say may have happened, could have happened, should have happened, whatever,
sentences.zh: 如果他们足够聪明，他们内心深处也必须意识到，他们所说的所有可能发生、应该发生、无论如何发生的事情，

sentences.en: was never proven.
sentences.zh: 从来都没有被证实过。

sentences.en: You think as more folks are brought into the system, they'll understand and appreciate that it works?
sentences.zh: 你认为随着更多人被引入这个系统，他们会理解并欣赏它的运作吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I've had major Trump supporters and believe that the election was stolen, that went and worked the polls.
sentences.zh: 我遇到过主要的特朗普支持者，他们相信选举被窃取了，但他们还是去投票站工作了。

sentences.en: And verified, yeah, we have a pretty good system.
sentences.zh: 并且证实了，是的，我们有一个相当不错的系统。

sentences.en: And she's actually kind of heartened that some of the more skeptical Republican voters in the state have this year become involved in the midterm elections,
sentences.zh: 她实际上感到有些欣慰，因为州内一些比较怀疑的共和党选民今年参与了中期选举，

sentences.en: either to monitor the polls or to work at the polls.
sentences.zh: 无论是去监督投票还是在投票站工作。

sentences.en: And Senator Bernier thinks the more people become involved in the system, the more they'll believe in the system and the less they'll doubt the system.
sentences.zh: 伯尼尔参议员认为，参与系统的人越多，他们就越会相信这个系统，对系统的怀疑就会越少。

sentences.en: Eventually, I did sign up to become a poll worker for the spring primaries.
sentences.zh: 最终，我确实报名成为了春季初选的投票站工作人员。

sentences.en: And Nikki is one of the people who tried to do just that.
sentences.zh: 尼基（Nikki）就是试图这样做的人之一。

sentences.en: I wanted to see for myself what happens.
sentences.zh: 我想亲眼看看发生了什么。

sentences.en: Because, you know, I don't like to just take somebody's word for it.
sentences.zh: 因为，你知道，我不喜欢只听信别人的话。

sentences.en: She signed up to be a poll worker in Racine County for this year's primaries.
sentences.zh: 她报名参加了今年拉辛县（Racine County）初选的投票站工作。

sentences.en: And as part of that, she went to a training.
sentences.zh: 作为其中的一部分，她参加了一次培训。

sentences.en: So it was City Hall.
sentences.zh: 地点是在市政厅。

sentences.en: And she remembers hearing the county clerk laying out the ground rules for how the training would work.
sentences.zh: 她记得听到县书记官制定了培训如何进行的规则。

sentences.en: She was the one kind of running everything.
sentences.zh: 她算是负责统筹一切的人。

sentences.en: So she stood up and kind of laid out everything for everybody.
sentences.zh: 所以她站起来，为每个人梳理了一切。

sentences.en: I think she had mentioned at least once that, you know, you need to be objective.
sentences.zh: 我想她至少提到过一次，你知道，你需要保持客观。

sentences.en: We're not talking about our political opinions with anybody.
sentences.zh: 我们不和任何人谈论我们的政治观点。

sentences.en: We're just here to assist people in their voting.
sentences.zh: 我们只是在这里协助人们投票。

sentences.en: So then we got in line.
sentences.zh: 然后我们就排起了队。

sentences.en: Eventually, they all get into a line.
sentences.zh: 最终，他们都排成了一队。

sentences.en: They hold their own mock election so that they can learn what a poll worker does at each step of the process.
sentences.zh: 他们举行了自己的模拟选举，这样他们就能学习投票站工作人员在流程的每一步要做什么。

sentences.en: I went there by myself, so I didn't know anybody there.
sentences.zh: 我是独自一人去的，所以我谁也不认识。

sentences.en: And so I wasn't having communication with anybody, but I was just listening to what was going on.
sentences.zh: 所以我没有和任何人交流，我只是在听发生了什么。

sentences.en: And it was loud enough that I could hear people expressing their opinions about how they felt about the election one way or the other.
sentences.zh: 声音大到我能听到人们表达他们对选举的看法，无论是哪种观点。

sentences.en: I mean, it was I heard both opinions of, like, the election was fine, everything was fine, and people are making a big deal out of nothing, you know,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我听到了两种观点，比如选举没问题，一切都很好，人们是在小题大做，你知道，

sentences.en: that would never happen in Wisconsin.
sentences.zh: 那种事在威斯康星州永远不会发生。

sentences.en: And then there was the other, you know, opinion of lack of confidence in the process and how, you know,
sentences.zh: 然后还有另一种，你知道，对程序缺乏信心的观点，以及他们如何，你知道，

sentences.en: they want to be a part to make sure that everything happens justly for everybody.
sentences.zh: 他们想参与其中，确保一切对每个人来说都是公正的。

sentences.en: Now, mind you, I was there for my own reason, but I still don't think it was appropriate for me to express that in that environment.
sentences.zh: 现在，请注意，我是出于自己的原因去的，但我仍然认为在那种环境下表达这些是不合适的。

sentences.en: I mean, these are the people that are going to be working the polls.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这些人可是要负责投票站工作的人。

sentences.en: It's not professional.
sentences.zh: 这不专业。

sentences.en: You should be professional, I think.
sentences.zh: 我认为你应该保持专业。

sentences.en: So if people were doing it at the training, do people do it why people go and vote?
sentences.zh: 所以如果人们在培训时就这样做，那人们去投票时也会这样吗？

sentences.en: It's just, I don't know.
sentences.zh: 只是，我不知道。

sentences.en: My feeling after I left was just not a good feeling.
sentences.zh: 我离开后的感觉并不好。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So the more Nikki saw, the less faith she had in the process,
sentences.zh: 所以尼基看到的越多，她对这个过程的信心就越少，

sentences.en: which is the exact opposite of what Senator Bernier had hoped would happen with skeptical Republicans participating in the process.
sentences.zh: 这与伯尼尔参议员希望怀疑论者共和党人参与该过程所产生的结果恰恰相反。

sentences.en: Yeah, the system as Senator Bernier had hoped it would operate didn't work and, in fact, did the opposite.
sentences.zh: 是的，伯尼尔参议员所希望的系统运作方式并没有奏效，事实上，结果适得其反。

sentences.en: In your mind, was it more about how elections are run or the people who are involved in them?
sentences.zh: 在你看来，这更多是关于选举的运作方式，还是关于参与其中的人？

sentences.en: Well, I think we can have a process and it could be done several different ways by whoever is leading that process.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为我们可以有一个流程，而且无论谁领导这个流程，都可以用几种不同的方式来完成。

sentences.en: So I guess I would say the people and my confidence in the people running the process is not there.
sentences.zh: 所以我猜我会说，是人，我对负责这个流程的人缺乏信心。

sentences.en: Do you feel like you're going to be able to trust the 2022 results?
sentences.zh: 你觉得你能够信任2022年的选举结果吗？

sentences.en: How are you thinking about that?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么想的？

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: We'll have to see.
sentences.zh: 我们拭目以待。

sentences.en: That's how I feel about it.
sentences.zh: 这就是我的感受。

sentences.en: And I assume you're going to physically go and vote this time again.
sentences.zh: 我假设你这次还会亲自去投票。

sentences.en: Oh, yes.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You know, when we look at the election today and we talk about democracy being on the ballot,
sentences.zh: 你知道，当我们审视今天的选举并谈论民主在选票上时，

sentences.en: we're not really talking about whether Tim Michaels wins or Tony Evers wins in Wisconsin or the next thing that happens about this bill or that bill.
sentences.zh: 我们并不是真的在谈论蒂姆·迈克尔斯还是托尼·埃弗斯（Tony Evers）在威斯康星州获胜，或者关于这个法案或那个法案的下一件事。

sentences.en: We're really hitting on what Nikki is talking about, which is a much more fundamental issue that's being confronted in Wisconsin and across the country
sentences.zh: 我们真正触及的是尼基所谈论的问题，这是一个在威斯康星州乃至全国范围内面临的更根本的问题，

sentences.en: about voters' faith in the elections themselves.
sentences.zh: 即选民对选举本身的信心。

sentences.en: And so that's what it means when people say that democracy is on the ballot, because the future of the faith in our elections is what's on the ballot in today's midterMs.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是人们说民主在选票上的含义，因为对我们选举的信心未来，正是今天中期选举中选票上所承载的内容。

sentences.en: Bovide, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 博维德（Bovide），非常感谢。

sentences.en: Thank you, Michael.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，迈克尔。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁了吗？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to The Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道你需要订阅《时报》才能访问所有的报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore The Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果你可以免费探索《时报》一个月，而无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download The New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在该应用中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间可以越过付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to The New York Times, download The Times app today and get free access for 30 days.

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know about today's election.
sentences.zh: 以下是你还需要了解的关于今天选举的其他信息。

sentences.en: Across the country on Tuesday, voters will cast ballots in 435 House races, 35 Senate races, and 36 Governor's races.
sentences.zh: 周二，全国各地的选民将在435场众议院选举、35场参议院选举和36场州长选举中投票。

sentences.en: To win control of the House, Republicans must pick up five seats from Democrats,
sentences.zh: 为了赢得众议院的控制权，共和党人必须从民主党人手中夺取五个席位，

sentences.en: a prospect seen as increasingly likely given historical patterns and polls showing growing Republican strength.
sentences.zh: 考虑到历史模式和民调显示共和党力量的增长，这一前景被认为越来越有可能实现。

sentences.en: To win control of the Senate, Republicans must pick up a single seat currently held by a Democrat, which may prove harder than winning back the House.
sentences.zh: 为了赢得参议院的控制权，共和党人必须夺取一个目前由民主党人持有的席位，这可能比夺回众议院更难。

sentences.en: Among the most closely watched Senate races are those in Pennsylvania, where recent polls show Democrat John Fetterman is deadlocked with Republican Mehmet Oz.
sentences.zh: 在最受关注的参议院竞选中，包括宾夕法尼亚州，最近的民调显示民主党人约翰·费特曼（John Fetterman）与共和党人穆罕默德·奥兹（Mehmet Oz）陷入僵局。

sentences.en: Nevada, where Democrat Catherine Cortez Masto is neck-and-neck with Republican Adam Laxalt.
sentences.zh: 内华达州，民主党人凯瑟琳·科尔特斯·马斯托（Catherine Cortez Masto）与共和党人亚当·拉克萨尔特（Adam Laxalt）势均力敌。
zh_words: 凯瑟琳·科尔特斯·马斯托

sentences.en: Georgia, where Democrat Raphael Warnock is nearly tied with Republican Herschel Walker.
sentences.zh: 佐治亚州，民主党人拉斐尔·沃诺克（Raphael Warnock）与共和党人赫歇尔·沃克（Herschel Walker）几乎打成平手。

sentences.en: And Ohio, where Democrat Tim Ryan is polling slightly behind Republican J.D.
sentences.zh: 以及俄亥俄州，民主党人蒂姆·瑞安（Tim Ryan）在民调中略微落后于共和党人J.D.

sentences.en: Vance.
sentences.zh: 万斯（Vance）。

sentences.en: Finally, governor's races will test the power of election denialism beyond Wisconsin.
sentences.zh: 最后，州长竞选将考验选举否认主义在威斯康星州之外的影响力。

sentences.en: In Arizona, polls show that Republican Carrie Lake, who denies that Donald Trump lost the 2020 election, is favored to prevail over Democrat Katie Hobbs,
sentences.zh: 在亚利桑那州，民调显示，否认唐纳德·特朗普输掉2020年大选的共和党人凯莉·莱克（Carrie Lake），有望战胜民主党人凯蒂·霍布斯（Katie Hobbs），

sentences.en: but that in Pennsylvania, another election denier, Republican Doug Mastriano, is widely expected to lose to Democrat Josh Shapiro.
sentences.zh: 但在宾夕法尼亚州，另一位选举否认者、共和党人道格·马斯特里亚诺（Doug Mastriano）被广泛预计将输给民主党人乔什·夏皮罗（Josh Shapiro）。

sentences.en: Results from the election will begin rolling in around 8 p.m.
sentences.zh: 选举结果将于今晚东部时间8点左右开始陆续公布。
